question: Does @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent import cleanly under Bun, and does a real Pi session natively write its JSONL transcript into a redirected session dir (no copy/symlink shim)?

checks.name: pi-imports-under-bun
checks.detail: `import * as pi from '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'` under Bun 1.3.14 yielded 144 named exports with no import-time error. The 2 blocked postinstalls (protobufjs, @google/genai) are transitive AI-provider scripts and are not needed to import Pi.

checks.name: native-transcript-capture-to-redirected-dir
checks.detail: SessionManager.create(cwd, sessionDir) targeted an absolute redirected dir (usesDefaultSessionDir=false). After a synthetic user+assistant exchange, Pi natively wrote <ISO>_<uuidv7>.jsonl at exactly getSessionFile(): isFile=true, isSymbolicLink=false, 3 entries [session, message(user), message(assistant)]. Read back through the public parseSessionEntries loader -> 3 entries. No copy or symlink involved.

checks.name: session-dir-redirect-documented
checks.detail: `pi --help` documents `--session-dir <dir>` and env var `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` ("overridden by --session-dir"). Env var is built at runtime as `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, which is why it is not a string literal in dist.

apiSurfaceFindings.finding: loadEntriesFromFile is NOT a public export in 0.80.7 (it exists internally). Public loader surface: parseSessionEntries(content: string): FileEntry[], migrateSessionEntries(...), getLatestCompactionEntry(entries). SC #7 ("loader-only JSONL reads, no hand JSON.parse") maps to: read the file bytes then use parseSessionEntries/migrateSessionEntries — never JSON.parse a .jsonl directly.

newSession({withSession}) is NOT a top-level export. Session creation is SessionManager.create(cwd, sessionDir, {id}) (+ instance newSession(options)), or the higher-level createAgentSession(...)/createAgentSessionFromServices(...). SessionManager statics: create, open, continueRecent, inMemory, forkFrom, list, listAll.

SessionManager buffers entries in memory and only writes the .jsonl on the first assistant message (_persist gates on hasAssistant; opens with 'wx' then append-only). A crashed session with no assistant response yet leaves NO file on disk. Session id is uuidv7; filename is <ISO>_<uuidv7>.jsonl (matches spec §1).
First entry is a `session` header entry (type: 'session'); message entries follow as { type: 'message', message: { role, content }, id, parentId, timestamp }.
apiSurfaceFindings.affects: boundary parsing of transcript entries (later commits)

notes: Live end-to-end launch through a real model turn was not exercised (no provider API key configured in this environment). It is unnecessary for this gate: the native persistence path (SessionManager._persist -> openSync 'wx') is identical whether the assistant message originates from a live model or a synthetic append, so writing the transcript into the redirected dir is proven either way. A model-driven end-to-end run is covered later by acceptance/sc-2 (Task 5, Commit 3).
